sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 of the 1900 Sanborn Hudson County series covers the western, uphill end of Guttenberg along its border with North Bergen, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right of the page. The sheet runs from Hudson Boulevard (today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard), which crosses the top in a curve, down through Eighth, Seventh, Sixth and Fifth Streets to Bergenline Avenue along the bottom. The cross streets are Hudson Avenue on the left and Hermann Avenue in the middle; the right edge follows the dashed boundary between Guttenberg and North Bergen, and the blocks beyond it, on the left beyond Hudson Avenue and above the Boulevard are left blank as outlines keyed to sheets 51, 122, 133, 137 and 131. The area is a newly subdivided residential district: long rows of narrow 25-foot lots, most of them still vacant, with scattered one- to three-storey frame dwellings, many with shingled or tin roofs, and small stables and sheds at the rear. The largest institution is St. Joseph's R.C. Church with its bell tower, and St. Joseph's R.C. School across the block, both between Seventh and Sixth Streets east of Hermann Avenue. Fifth Street toward Bergenline Avenue is more closely built, with a hay and feed store, a bowling alley and a blacksmith near the corner of Hermann and Bergenline Avenues. A large block between the Boulevard and Eighth Street east of Hermann Avenue is mostly open ground with a few buildings. Fire hydrants and water mains with their sizes are marked along the streets. A small note in the bottom margin points to Franklin Avenue, which begins on the next sheet.
notes: Hudson Boulevard is today's John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Eighth, Seventh, Sixth and Fifth Streets are today's Adams, Jackson, Polk and Madison Streets.
Hudson Avenue is today's 68th Street; Hermann Avenue is today's 70th Street.
St. Joseph's R.C. Church and St. Joseph's R.C. School stand between Seventh and Sixth Streets east of Hermann Avenue.
Printed scale is 1 inch = 60 feet.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 of the 1900 Sanborn Hudson County series covers the central part of Guttenberg and the edge of West New York, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Bergenline Avenue runs across the top of the page, Fourth Street (today Palisade Avenue) across the middle and Third Street (today Hudson Avenue) along the bottom. Up the page run Twenty-Third Street on the left, then Hudson, Franklin and Hermann Avenues. The dashed boundary between West New York and Guttenberg runs through the long block east of Twenty-Third Street, and the streets of West New York, Palisade Avenue and Hudson Avenue, are lettered in the left margin where they meet Twenty-Third Street, offset from Guttenberg's streets. Blocks beyond the sheet are blank outlines keyed to sheets 51, 52, 53, 56 and 131. The district is residential, with rows of narrow lots lined by two- and three-storey frame houses, many with stores or flats, along Bergenline Avenue and Hudson Avenue, and a scattering of houses elsewhere. Along Bergenline Avenue are Engine Co. No. 1 and Hose Co. No. 4, a bakery with its oven, and a blacksmith; a wheelwright, stable and shed stand near Hermann Avenue, and a sash, doors and blinds shop and a carpenter's and paint shop occur in the western blocks. Institutions are the German Baptist Mission between Bergenline Avenue and Fourth Street, and a Presbyterian church and a public school in the block between Fourth and Third Streets west of Franklin Avenue, which also holds a wagon shed and stable. Hydrants, water mains and street widths of 50 and 80 feet are marked.
notes: Fourth Street is today's Palisade Avenue and Third Street today's Hudson Avenue.
Twenty-Third Street is today's 67th Street; Hudson, Franklin and Hermann Avenues are today's 68th, 69th and 70th Streets.
The margin labels Palisade Ave. and Hudson Ave. are West New York streets meeting Twenty-Third Street; they continue today as Palisade and Hudson Avenues with a jog at 67th Street.
Engine Co. No. 1 and Hose Co. No. 4 on Bergenline Avenue; German Baptist Mission; Presbyterian church; public school.
Printed scale is 1 inch = 60 feet.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 of the 1900 Sanborn Hudson County series covers Guttenberg between Third Street and Bullsferry Road, with a strip of West New York on the left, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Third Street (today Hudson Avenue) runs across the top, Second Street (today Broadway) across the middle and Bullsferry Road (today Park Avenue) along the bottom; up the page run Twenty-Third Street, Hudson Avenue, Franklin Avenue and Hermann Avenue. The dashed boundary between West New York and Guttenberg runs through the block east of Twenty-Third Street, and West New York's Hudson Avenue, Dewey Avenue and Broadway are lettered in the left margin, Dewey Avenue drawn as a diagonal street meeting Twenty-Third Street. Neighbouring blocks are blank outlines keyed to sheets 53, 54, 55, 58 and 125. The blocks are long and narrow, divided into 25-foot lots, and only partly built: frame dwellings of one to three storeys stand along the avenues, with outbuildings behind, and the large interior blocks between Second Street and Bullsferry Road are mostly vacant. Along Bullsferry Road the frontage is closer built, with stores and dwellings, a bakery and a stable. Smaller works include a carpenter's shop near Twenty-Third Street and a kerosene oil engine bottler on Franklin Avenue; an insurance office stands on Bullsferry Road east of Franklin Avenue. Hydrants, water mains and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are marked.
notes: Third Street is today's Hudson Avenue, Second Street today's Broadway, and Bullsferry Road today's Park Avenue.
Twenty-Third Street is today's 67th Street; Hudson, Franklin and Hermann Avenues are today's 68th, 69th and 70th Streets.
Hudson Ave., Dewey Ave. and Broadway in the left margin are West New York streets meeting Twenty-Third Street.
Printed scale is 1 inch = 60 feet.

Dewey Avenue and Broadway of West New York in the left margin.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 of the 1900 Sanborn Hudson County series covers the eastern end of Guttenberg at the edge of the Palisades, with a strip of West New York on the left, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Bullsferry Road (today Park Avenue) runs across the top, First Street (today Bellevue Avenue) across the middle, and Hudson Boulevard East (today Boulevard East) curves along the bottom; up the page run Twenty-Third Street, Hudson Avenue, Franklin Avenue and Hermann Avenue. The dashed boundary between West New York and Guttenberg runs through the block east of Twenty-Third Street, and West New York's Lincoln Place and Washington Place are lettered in the left margin. Neighbouring blocks are blank outlines keyed to sheets 56, 57, 78, 79 and 126; the area below the Boulevard is left blank apart from the north arrow and the scale. This sheet holds the town's civic centre: the Town Hall with Hose Co. No. 1 and Hook and Ladder No. 1 on Bullsferry Road, Washington Hall near Twenty-Third Street, and the Franklin Club with bowling alleys and a stable on Hudson Avenue. The largest works is the Standard Brewery on Bullsferry Road at Hermann Avenue, with a cooling room, stable and open shed, beside a hall with bowling alley and stage. A small wood turning shop stands in the same block. The rest is residential, with frame houses of one to three storeys on narrow lots and short lots facing the Boulevard. Hydrants, water mains and street widths of 50, 60 and 80 feet are marked.
notes: Bullsferry Road is today's Park Avenue, First Street today's Bellevue Avenue, and Hudson Boulevard East today's Boulevard East.
Twenty-Third Street is today's 67th Street; Hudson, Franklin and Hermann Avenues are today's 68th, 69th and 70th Streets.
Town Hall with Hose Co. No. 1 and Hook and Ladder No. 1; Washington Hall; Franklin Club; Standard Brewery.
